reviews.question: Is this a limited seven-crop screening prototype or a global crop recommender?
reviews.answer: The catalog contains 7 screening crops: Bush snap bean, Garden pea, Sweet corn, Radish, Tomato, Cabbage, Bulb onion. Its declared scope is: Seven starter vegetable types with regional US extension evidence. Local varieties, planting calendars and commercial-scale suitability are not globally validated. This supports describing it as a limited screening prototype; global map access is not global agronomic validation.

reviews.question: Can the demo country generate valid alternatives?
reviews.answer: Saved screening coverage: SG: 2 (cabbage, tomato); IN: 5 (bush-bean, cabbage, onion, pea, tomato); AU: 6 (bush-bean, cabbage, onion, pea, sweet-corn, tomato); BR: 2 (onion, tomato); KH: 0 (none). Australia, India, Singapore and Brazil have at least two screened choices; Cambodia does not. F01/F03 check the actual UI behavior.

reviews.question: Is real NASA POWER accessible to a fresh browser user, including CORS?
reviews.answer: Verified on the local preview only; public-origin CORS still requires TEST_BASE_URL: a fresh isolated browser profile loaded the actual POWER response through the app worker; rendered metadata reports direct retrieval, units and its exact source URL. This is one observed run, not an availability guarantee.

Assumptions
One field; one crop starts each four-month slot; 12-month horizon.
Maturity upper bound plus 14 days for harvest and turnaround; remaining days are unallocated.
Every crop day uses the same month/day in 2025; windows wrap across the reference year. February 29 uses February 28 if absent.
What this comparison cannot conclude
Crop choices are filtered using national FAOSTAT 2020–2024 production categories for Australia; category/cultivar mappings and field suitability remain unverified.
Seven starter vegetable types with regional US extension evidence. Local varieties, planting calendars and commercial-scale suitability are not globally validated.
One historical year is not a forecast, climate normal, validated planting window or estimate of extreme-event likelihood.
No location is agronomically validated by this prototype, including the source region. Land use, altitude effects, cultivar, soil pH, salinity and economics need local verification.
Ideal-air exposure references exist for Garden pea, Cabbage. Heat exposure is unassessed for Bush snap bean, Sweet corn, Radish, Tomato, Bulb onion. Quantitative cold-survival rules are not modelled for Garden pea, Radish, Cabbage, Bulb onion; winter survival remains unassessed.
Nitrogen fixation and soil effects depend on rhizobia, residues and management. No soil improvement, fertilizer credit or pest prevention is predicted.
Maturity plus 14-day turnaround is a planning assumption; growing-degree days, harvest duration and photoperiod are unmodelled. Unallocated slot time needs a locally chosen cover/management plan.
Rain-free exposure is the longest sequence of exact zero PRECTOTCORR days within a crop window; missing rain breaks a run and is counted separately. It is a historical exposure indicator, not crop water demand, effective rain or savings.
No soil-test pH supplied. Crop pH checks cannot run.
Irrigation is unknown; crop water sufficiency cannot be assessed.
Soil type and soil tests are missing; nutrient and drainage suitability cannot be established.
Pest history and multi-year rotations are missing; disease or pest-cycle impacts cannot be established.
Previous crop is unspecified; family carryover before the first slot cannot be checked.
